text: 5 and the use of spironolactone should therefore be considered in such patients.6-8 A small study9 has also shown benefit in patients with less severe heart failure. However, use of spironolactone with ACE inhibitors may lead to hyperkalaemia and careful monitoring of potassium concentrations is required10,11 (see Interactions, above). A retrospective analysis12 of heart failure patients found that over 10% had to stop spironol- actone because of hyperkalaemia, and a further 10% stopped be- cause of worsening renal function. Risk factors were advanced age and higher baseline plasma-potassium concentrations. 1. Tang WHW, et al. Aldosterone receptor antagonists in the med- ical management of chronic heart failure.
